Lake Volta. The world's largest artificial reservoir by surface area, Lake Volta was created by the Akosombo Dam on the Volta River in Ghana, covering approximately three thousand two hundred eighty-three square miles. It has been central to Ghana's economic development since its completion in nineteen sixty-five, providing hydroelectric power, transportation, and fisheries.

The lake was created by damming the White Volta River, a major West African waterway, in southeastern Ghana. Though it is the world's largest artificial lake by surface area, Lake Baikal in Russia and some other natural lakes are vastly larger by volume. The lake supplies hydroelectric power for Ghana and neighboring nations, historically providing over ninety percent of Ghana's electricity generation.

The reservoir created one of West Africa's most productive freshwater fisheries, supporting tens of thousands of fishermen. However, the dam's construction required the displacement of over eighty thousand people from towns and villages flooded by the rising reservoir. The lake's creation had significant environmental effects, including altered downstream flow regimes that affected the Volta Delta. Tourism and recreation on Lake Volta have become increasingly important to Ghana's economy.
